Q1: Which `job_workflow_ref` values should the broker accept for `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/.github/workflows/<exact allowlisted file>`?
Choices:
A) `@refs/heads/main`, plus a 40-hex SHA pin that the broker checks (via `job_workflow_sha`) is reachable from protected `main`/`stable` or equals a release tag. Anything else is refused, and the check fails closed if verification is unavailable. (RECOMMENDED)
B) `@refs/heads/main` and `@refs/heads/stable` only, with every SHA pin refused. **Note:** this breaks every consumer repo, because their installed wrappers call `@<sha> # stable`. All their Claude roles would fall back to codex.
C) `@refs/heads/main`, plus a SHA pin only when it equals the current `stable` tag commit. Consumers that haven't synced the latest release would fall back to codex until `update_workflows.yml` updates their pin.
Q2: In coding-workflows itself, how should a run whose workflow is dispatched from a non-`main` branch be handled? Examples: `claude-engine-smoke.yml` run from a feature branch, or `security-audit.yml` dispatched with `--ref <PR branch>` by the single-issue security pass.
Choices:
A) Refuse it with a 403 reason code, so the job takes the existing codex fallback (`AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK ... reason=no_credential`). This is the finding's own recommendation. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Allow it only if its `job_workflow_sha` also passes the Q1 check (the commit is already on protected `main`/`stable`). **Note:** with Q1:B or Q1:C this gives the same result as A.
C) Keep accepting any ref for coding-workflows itself and tighten only consumer callers. This leaves the reported exploit open for this repository.
